text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
HELSINGIN SANOMAT
- A majority of Finns consider narrowing income gaps important, a poll by Suomen Gallup shows.
- MPs have to start acting better to restore the legislature's prestige, says Speaker Riitta Uosukainen, commenting on recent controversy.
- Finnish food, feed and chemicals group Raision Tehtaat Oy to stop buying genetically manipulated soya next year, giving in to public protest. @
- Cooperative EKA which is in debt restructuring must cut deposits over 200 markka by 71 per cent, Supreme Court rules.
TURUN SANOMAT

- Insurance broker Unibro Sijoituspalvely says a transfer of Suomi-Salama's insurance portfolio to Pohjola would not benefit policy holders and proposes that Suomi-Salama make use of its 39 percent vote or start selling Pohjola shares.
AAMULEHTI
- Finns' confidence in the judicial system, parliament, civil servants and big corporations is recovering after a fall in the late 1980s, poll by Suomen Gallup shows. @

- Finnish insurers are setting up a 'blacklist' of people who have attempted insurance fraud. The list would include about 1,000-2,000 names, says spokesman at the Federation of Finnish Insurance Companies.
KAUPPALEHTI
- The Helsinki Stock Exchange is unfazed by Swedish plans to merge the Stockholm bourse with derivatives exchange OM Gruppen and create a financial centre backed by the state. @
- Finnish investment banks Mandatum, Merita Corporate Finance and Conventum will have to compete harder in mergers and acquisitions market, say their fees are not excessive.
- Valmet Dura -- paper machine maker Valmet 's joint venture with Japanese Yamauchi -- opened a new plant in Jarvenpaa in southern Finland on Monday.
- Distorted farming income data shows strong growth, Pellervo Institute of Economic Research says, fearing farmers may lose subsidies. @
- Petrol sales fell last year, and the price has risen too much due to taxes, says Georg Tallberg, managing director of Shell in Finland.
- Tamrock has in three years become market leader in three segments of mining equipment in southern Africa. It is second in all other segments and closing the gap.

- Strong growth in traditional consumer electronics sales slowed clearly in January-March, but the volume of mobile phone wholesales grew 40 percent year-on-year, electronics wholesalers lobby says. @
HUFVUDSTADSBLADET

- Finance ministry finance director Kari Nars was appointed board member of the European Bank of Reconstruction and Development (EBRD). A successor at the ministry has not yet been appointed, Inga-Maria Grohn to do the job temporarily.
- Engineering group Rauma's strength is having four divisions with different business cycles, managing director Heikki Hakala says.
